utterances.text: In the next two documents, that's tab 4 and tab 5, it's actually an invitation, the same invitations from the 18 February 1992, and on the document, tab 5, there is a handwritten note saying, "Mrgud, come along." "Mrgud," is that your nickname or was that your nickname?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was my nickname.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next exhibit, tab 6 in that same binder, is your appointment as Assistant Minister of Defence, dated 19 December 1991. Did you provide Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. this document as well?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I provided it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next document, tab 7 in that binder, is a specification of requirements for the work of the Serbian National Security Service, signed by Stevo Bogic, and subsequently also a different signature underneath. What was Bogic's nickname? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that Bogic's nickname was Jajo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's not indicated in the proofing summary, but Mr. Mrgud has mentioned this person and his role and also the role of this Serbian National Security Service in paragraph 37, so I will not ask any more questions in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In -- you mentioned in your statement, in paragraph 103, that in relation to the southern part of the Krajina, the connections -- the close connections of Mr. Milosevic were Milan Babic and Milan Martic. How do you know that, and -- yes, how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were connections between the people you mentioned. I mean, they are generally known through the media and from time to time, I would hear from Martic or Babic themselves that they were meeting with Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next -- the next chapter in your statement is the forming of the RSK. You have described in the statement the formation of the RSK, and we need not go into details. You have actually listed in the statement the members of the RSK government.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, it's tab 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you look -- Mr. Milanovic, if you look at your binder with the exhibits, you will find there tab 8. Is that the list that you actually made about the ministers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you mentioned in your statement, in paragraph 92 and 93, you mentioned the meeting in Borovo Selo on the 26th of February, 1992, and you listed those from the Serbian government being present there. Did they influence the decisions being taken on that day? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think they did not influence the decision-making on that day, but their presence meant something as support to that Assembly meeting being held in Borovo Selo on that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Turning now to the next three tabs in that binder. It's tab 9, tab 10, and tab 11. These three documents deal with your position as Assistant Minister of Defence of the SAO. What were your duties in this function?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: My duties in this function were the duties that any ministry in any country has, and especially that particular Ministry of Defence. Under wartime conditions or conditions of imminent threat of war, the ministry had to take care of the army, its rear, supplies, logistics, and the safety of the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In tab 9, that's the first decision on your appointment signed by Stojan Spanovic, there is a reference made to an approval by the General Staff of the VJ. Can you explain why such an approval was needed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was needed because at the time in the former Yugoslavia, the Ministry of Defence mostly consisted of military men who were employed in the General Staff or in the Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. So that in my opinion, that is why this was needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in tab 11 - that's the decision from the 30th of October, 1995 - there is again the reference to the VJ, and actually, it says here that you were a civilian member of the VJ. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I was not an active-duty officer of the army of Yugoslavia, I was admitted as a civilian employed by the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But you are actually in the RSK and now, according to this document and to what you say, you become a civilian employee of the VJ. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: It is well known that officers of the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina were active-duty officers of the army of Yugoslavia and that they were deployed and assigned to work in the Republic of Serbian Krajina, or they went there voluntarily, and they received their salaries from the army of Yugoslavia. Since the Ministry of Defence is a specific body that is closely linked to the army, the decision was taken that all the people in the Defence Ministry of the Republic of Serbian Krajina should be employees of the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In tab 11, in this document we're talking about, there is mention of a military post number 4001. What kind of post was that? Where was it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: It is a military post that concerned itself with these officers and civilians in the army of Yugoslavia who were located in the territory of the former Republic of Serbian Krajina, and it was located in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: While you maintained the position of Assistant Minister of Defence of the RSK through those years, were you always employed by the VJ under the said post?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true, right up until about the end of 1995 or the beginning of 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you always paid by the VJ? Did you get a salary?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was there a similar post as you had in relation to the southern part of the Krajina? That's Knin area.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think there was. I think there was another one or two assistants.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were also employed and paid by the VJ, like you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think they were. One of them was also a civilian like me, and the other one was an active-duty officer of the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you know their names?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: The active military officer was Lieutenant Colonel Dusko Babic, and the civilian person was Milan Potusa.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Milanovic, you also provided a document, this tab 12 in the binder, an invitation to a meeting in Knin on the 30th of May, 1994. Are you actually -- your position and you in person, are you actually addressed under position number 15, saying, "Heads of the Ministry of Defence Departments of Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, and Western Srem"? Is that addressed to you, this position?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: One could say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You described the TO and its structure and the cooperation with the JNA in your statement, and it's in various paragraphs mentioned, in particular in the paragraphs 17 and 21. We do not need to repeat that, but my question to you is: Was the TO subordinated to the JNA during military actions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Always.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you, you not only in person but the Ministry of Defence or Stojicic Badza, did you have meetings before military activities with the JNA officers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, I didn't have a position, but I do know that Badza held meetings with the command of the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Where were such meetings held?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: That depended, but mostly in the territory of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Perhaps sometimes also within the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned in your statement also that the TO of Serbia was somehow involved, and you mention in particular the Generals Mandaric and Geza Farkas. Why were they involved in the military activities in Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem? What was their role?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Their role was simple: Wherever the army of Yugoslavia is participating, it is normal for the TO to participate as well as it is, in a sense, within the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Does that mean that the TO -- TO units from Serbia participated in your region, or what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it means, they participated.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In your statement, in paragraph 50, you have addressed the strength of the troops of the JNA being present in your region, and you mention the Novi Sad Corps and later the Guards Brigade. When did the Guards Brigade arrive? Can you say?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say exactly, but I think that the Guards Brigade came to the area of Srem sometime around August 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you prepare a map indicating the zones of responsibility of the Guards Brigade and the -- and the Novi Sad Corps?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's now a map, and it would be Exhibit 326. That's the map binder of Croatia. And the next tab number would be 30. I'm just told it's 30.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you actually produce this map and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I should correct; it should be 31.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: 31. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 30 is, I wrote it, related to that Agotic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have indicated in this map the ethnic composition in the villages of the region, and it explains itself. We do not need to go into details, but could you show us on the ELMO where the different units, JNA units were, and what was the line?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: In the territory of Baranja, one or two brigades were involved of the Novi Sad Corps, who also came sometime in August to Baranja. In the territory of Slavonia, the Novi Sad Corps participated with several brigades, and they also arrived sometime in August in the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. territory of Vukovar, but it must be noted that a part of the army of Yugoslavia that were in Vukovar, a smaller unit, joined them, joined the Novi Sad Corps. And in the territory of Srem, the Guards Brigade was active, which in a later stage grew into a corps. Now, whether it was called the Belgrade or Guards Corps, I don't know, but at first it was just a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And if I understand your drawing correctly, the border between the Novi Sad Corps region and the Guards Brigade, that's the blue line, the blue line following a river?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is the blue line, and the river is Vuka, which divided the town of Vukovar into two.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's -- that should be enough with the map. Your Honour, just to clarify this, I'm just told that you have actually two maps. The one is -- the bigger -- the map showing the bigger region shows the entire SAO, while the map showing the smaller region is more precise and shows Eastern Slavonia and Srem while the other one includes also Baranja, and in the Baranja region the witness has not indicated the ethnic composition of the villages because it didn't really matter for this case. That's the distinction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The next number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 326, tab 32.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have in tab 30 or tab 31 any map, and I see that there's quite a number of them here. So could you please give me one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The accused should have the maps.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I apologise. I didn't -- I wasn't aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I remember that I asked you to update the index of the map binder and its table of contents.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We will take care of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit 326, 343.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Milanovic, you have mentioned the role of the JNA as being one of a buffer between the two parties in the region. Did the JNA mission change in August 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In August 1991, its role changed, the role of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In which way?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Roughly at that time, the JNA from the buffer zone crossed over to the Serb side, but I must clarify that briefly, because in those days, Croats were fleeing and leaving the JNA and other ethnic groups as well, and the JNA was replenished with Serbs so that it de facto crossed to the Serb side, because it was virtually of the same ethnic composition.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness's microphone be switched on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did JNA units from then onwards conduct joint operations with the TO brigade -- brigades?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did act together.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did volunteers from Serbia participate in these joint actions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: There weren't many volunteers, but they did participate.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were there any volunteers from Montenegro, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't really guarantee that there were some from Montenegro. They were mostly from Serbia in my area, according to the best of my knowledge. Maybe in some other part of Krajina or Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How were these volunteers integrated into the troops? Under which subordination were they?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: In most cases the volunteers were under the command of the Territorial Defence, and the Territorial Defence was under the command of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned in your statement that Arkan's Tigers also participated in joint operations. How were they subordinated within the troops?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: The Tigers were subordinated to the TO, and the TO, as I have said, to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did police units from the RS -- from the region participate in the joint military actions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: They did, yes. They participated in joint actions, again under the command of the TO and the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did police units from Serbia, from the MUP Serbia participate?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say units. There were individuals, but units did not participate in active combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In paragraph 17 and 21 of your statement, and it's also 21 in the proofing summary, you have described military actions in Nova Tenja, and we need not address that, you mentioned that Radovan Stojicic Badza planned and commanded the operation jointly, and I wonder what exactly does that mean? What did he do in relation to Nova Tenja?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Radovan Stojicic Badza as the commander of the Territorial Defence, it was normal that he should participate in the planning and commanding in the liberation of Nova Tenja together with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who was then the commander on the ground who actually directed the troops during the military action?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say the army, you mean the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: All troops. All troops involved. Who directed then the actions in the field? Was Badza then in the field or who was there in charge?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that Badza and General Bijorcevic were in command of that operation, and they were at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, do I need to lead all evidence in relation to Badza which is now coming in the paragraphs 23 and the following live or can I restrict on additional evidence given by the witness during the proofing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If it relates to the accused and it's evidence about his acts and conduct, then you must call it live.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Then I just simply make the distinction between Badza's action in the field and his relationship with Mr. Milosevic, I think. I'll make the distinction here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have described Radovan Stojicic's arrival in the region in your statement, and you have also described him as being the commander of the TO in the region. My question is: Did he come as a volunteer to the region or was he there as an official from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that he did not come as a volunteer.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why do you think that? What are your observations to that effect?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: He never said that he had come as a volunteer, and on the ground, our understanding was that he had been sent there by the official authorities of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You described how he arrived with personnel from the MUP Serbia and also with MUP Serbia equipment. Did he continue to receive equipment from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Partially, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did he continue to receive his salary from MUP Serbia? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have mentioned in paragraphs 19 and 24 also Zivko Trajkovic and Miodrag Zavisic. How long did Zivko Trajkovic stay in the region?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that Zivko Trajkovic stayed in the area up until the time when the blue helmets arrived in the area of Baranja and Srem and Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Miodrag Zavisic, how long did he stay?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: For as long as Trajkovic did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In paragraph 28 of your statement, and it's 25 in the summary, you mention also inspector Veljko Bogunovic who came with about 100 men, Serb policemen employed by the MUP. For how long did they stay in the region?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Also until the blue helmets arrived in the region.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Given Badza's role and responsibility, does that mean he and his followers or successors were in charge of both the TO and the police in the entire region?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: In a sense and pursuant to the law on the imminent threat of war and in a state of war, the police as an armed force comes under the Territorial Defence so that de facto Badza was the commander of the police as well. Only Zavisic was in charge of the professional activities of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: After Badza's and Trajkovic's return to Serbia, who then took over the role as the TO commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: The role of the TV commander was taken over by Colonel Bogdan Sladojevic, but through the Vance Plan and the arrival of the Blue Helmets, the Territorial Defence was partially or almost entirely disbanded and the equipment and weapons went under the system of a double lock, double key.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Colonel Sladojevic, was he a JNA officer, and did he continue to be an officer in the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Sladojevic was an officer of the army of Yugoslavia, and he stayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next exhibit is one that we have already had in the courtroom. It's tab -- it's Exhibit 466, tab 12, and I just would like you to have a look at it. Is that an authentic document, and do you know the signature of Mr. Stojicic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the document is authentic and that that is the signature of Radovan Stojicic. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, in tab 12, I have a document which was signed by -- or, rather, it's an invitation to a meeting. It was signed by a certain Kuzet. I can't find this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it is in a separate binder which was already introduced, which is together with the maps. The last document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's Exhibit 466 --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just got this with the maps now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's a device, Your Honours, it's a device just for everyone in the courtroom to find the exhibits easier. It's in Exhibit 466, tab 12, already known.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Milanovic, you said that the civilian authorities were more or less powerless at the -- when the war started and that the JNA was the main power in the region. In your statement, in paragraph 17, you, however, mentioned that the TO was put on a more equal footage when Badza arrived. Can you say when the TO was on a more equal footage, at what time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem was brought into a somewhat more equitable position when Radovan Stojicic Badza arrived. In some areas this happened in the month of October, and in other areas it happened towards the end of November too.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When this equal footage or somewhat equal footage, was that also achieved in the Vukovar region; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as the Vukovar region is concerned, it involved the month of November, the end of November, because one could not get from Slavonia to Vukovar by land because Vukovar was still under Croatian authority. So as for the lower part of Srem where the town of Vukovar is for the most part, on the right bank of the Vuka river, this was under the command of the then JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when you say the end of November, does that mean after the fall of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did Stojicic and the TO become even more powerful than the JNA at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think so. After the Vukovar operations were completed, the Territorial Defence gained in importance, like the civilian authorities a bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have described in your statement how you met Badza Stojicic and your dealings with him. When did you meet him for the first time, and did you ask -- did he ask anything of you at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that I met him sometime during the first part of the month of October 1991, and yes, he did ask me, because he had come from the area of Serbia. He was not familiar with this area, and he had heard from other people that I was familiar with the area, so he wanted me to come along with him when he was carrying out his duties. He wanted me to be in the same car with him so that I would show him the way, because this was not a good time, it was a time of war.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did he ask you information regarding the villages and their ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. That among other things.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you become friends with him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you continue to be close to him even after he left the region?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned Badza's activities and that he also took part in government session. What -- was his word -- what he said, did this count in the region?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did. It did carry weight.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was he well-informed about what was going on in the region?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think he was well-informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why do you think that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that because I spent quite a bit of time with him. I think he had all information as to what was going on in the field, particularly because he was commander of the Territorial Defence, and he had meetings every day with his co-workers who were throughout the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Stojicic reported back to Belgrade; and if so, to whom?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that he sent reports to Belgrade, but I don't know who to.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have now an exhibit, and it's tab 13 in the binder, in the first binder, Exhibit 549, and is that a document that you provided? It's a decision dealing with a pistol. Is that what you provided?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not -- I'm not quite sure that I'm the person who provided that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: If you have a look at this document, you see there a number on top of it, MM-VD-07. Do you recall that documents that you provided were marked like this during the interview?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This document is a proper one.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not mentioned in the proofing summary, but the witness speaks about this document at paragraph 27 of his statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was Radovan Stojicic close to Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, according to my information, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did he communicate -- did Stojicic communicate directly with Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, after 1992, yes. As for 1991 and 1992, I cannot say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In the transcript it says as your answer: "As far as I know after 1992, yes." That means not in 1992? You're not sure about 1992? You can't say for 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say anything about 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How do you know that -- what information did you have that he was close to Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is information from Radovan Stojicic, Badza.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you actually hear -- overhear conversations that he had with Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did. As I've already said, I heard a few conversations.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How would Badza address Mr. Milosevic in these conversations?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Badza addressed him with respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what -- how would he -- would he address him by name, by title?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Always by his title.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how would in turn Mr. Milosevic address Stojicic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think he called him Badza.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In 1993, did the VJ withdraw elements from their positions at the border with the -- with Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And noticing that, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I informed Badza that that is what the army of Yugoslavia -- no, the JNA -- no, actually by then the army of Yugoslavia did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what did Badza do about this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Badza called Mr. Milosevic right there in front of me, and he informed him about the situation. Mr. Milosevic called Momcilo Perisic and told him to revert the situation to the way it was before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Could you hear what Mr. Milosevic was saying to Badza and subsequently to Mr. Perisic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I did hear it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How was that possible?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, quite simply Badza had the speaker phone on, so I heard Mr. Milosevic's voice. And Mr. Milosevic said to Badza to wait, that he would call Momcilo now, meaning Perisic. He did call him, and he told him to return the troops where they had been before. I heard that too, because the speaker phone was still on, and the army was indeed returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you also have an occasion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think it's about time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milanovic, we're going to have a break now for 20 minutes. During this adjournment and any others there may be in your evidence, please don't speak to anybody about it until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. We will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you just described to us the conversation in which Mr. Milosevic reversed the order by Momcilo Perisic. Do you recall what exactly he said?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic said to General Perisic, "Momcilo, it's not for you to think. Just return the troops to where they had been."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You also described a conversation between Mr. Stojicic and Milosevic in relation to a demonstration in Serbia. Can you tell the Court what you heard on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: During the demonstrations in Serbia, Radovan Stojicic Badza was in my apartment. He called Mr. Milosevic, and they spoke about the current situation regarding the demonstrations.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Milanovic, you described the role of Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan in the region, and we do not need to repeat all this. My question is: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. When Badza left the region, to whom was Arkan then subordinated?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Legally, he was subordinated to the commander of the Territorial Defence, which soon after that or, rather, after the Vance Plan, was transformed into the blue brigades of the police, the Milicija. Like the other territorials, the Tigers fell under the command of the blue brigades or the police, rather.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You say legally he was subordinated to the TO commander. And de facto? Is there a difference?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: That is difference, because the Territorial Defence withered away. According to the Vance Plan, it was only the command of the Territorial Defence that could have stayed on, and they were to coordinate with UN headquarters because all the heavy weapons were under the double-key provision, and the UN guarded all heavy weapons. And Bozo Kosutic took over the command of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What was Arkan's role after the fighting had ceased, if any?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: His role was the following: He had a unit that he commanded, and he was present in case there were attack of the Croatian army. Then he would defend the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned in your statement that Arkan became the commander of the training camp in Erdut and that it was Hadzic who appointed him to this position. Who made the decision to this effect? Who decided that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that decision was made by Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This training centre, what purpose did it have before Arkan moved in?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that centre was the centre for training the Territorial Defence of the former Yugoslavia. Right after the war operations started, sometime in the month of August, that is where the government of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem moved into. For a while, Radovan Stojicic Badza was staying there as well. When Arkan came, the TO command moved to another building in Erdut which was called the Saponija rest house. The government moved to the castle, as it was called. Others called it the yellow house. This centre remained the training centre for the TO, and that is where Arkan was accommodated. Afterwards, it was only Arkan's centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was the Arkan training centre financed by the DP Dalj company?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at that time in these uncertain, unstable times, the TO and the police were financed in different ways until proper government was established, when taxes were paid and when there was a budget once again. In the meantime, individual companies assisted the TO and the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So the answer, did DP Dalj finance the -- Arkan's training centre? You didn't --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you review during the proofing several exhibits dealing with the financing of the training centre, and did you find these documents authentic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the documents are authentic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's tab 14 of the Exhibit 549, the legal foundation for this financing. Tab 15 equally, a decree related to the legal foundation. Tab 16, a certificate related to the position of Milan Panisic as a director of the Dalj company. Then we have a document, tab 427 -- Exhibit 427, tab 44, which is in that separate bundle, and it is an approval that the expenses of the TO training centre be -- will be reimbursed by the Dalj enterprise, and that's you who signs it? Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And this document doesn't have a date on it. Do you recall when you approved this practice?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: This document doesn't have a date, but in the top left-hand corner there appears to be written when this company, DP Dalj, received the document, and it says in 1992. So I think this was sometime at the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And we have the tabs again from Exhibit 427, tab 47 and 45.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May. Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two binders for this witness. One -- in one, the last tab is 31, and in the other, the last tab is number 27. I don't have anywhere tabs 44, unless there is a third binder which I haven't seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. It's in this bundle, which is together with the maps.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the maps. This bundle says the Presidency of Yugoslavia, and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You noticed the number, exhibit number, on the left top of the document. These are exhibits which were already introduced. The exhibit we are dealing with now is Exhibit 427, which was introduced at the time that Mr. Torkildsen gave evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So we have the two invoices, one from January 1992 signed by Arkan, and then the other one from January -- January -- the 22nd of January, 1992. Are they authentic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: They are.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Then we have three documents, that's tab 45, again in the Exhibit 549. Tab 45, tab 17, tab 18, and tab 19 related to the payment of specific invoices. And I don't think we need to go into details to this effect. And finally, we have tab 20, and it relates to -- again to the payment, and my question to you would be: Were payments facilitated through accounts in Serbia, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: With the beginning of the war operations and the fact that Croatia failed to recognise the country and the abolition of the system of payments transactions that used to apply in the former Republic of Croatia, there were quite a number of work organisations or companies working in the territory of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, and they opened their accounts in banks in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the government as such, the SAO government as such, we have here also indicated on page 4 in the English translation that there is an account for the budget of the Serbian district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem with Mr. Hadzic as the person who is able to make transactions. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that document and that decision, and it is pursuant to that decision that companies in the region of Srem and Baranja opened accounts in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Turning now to tab 21 of the Exhibit 549, there is a photo, Mr. Milanovic. Who is seen on the photo, and can you say where this photo was made?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: On the photograph is Radovan Stojicic Badza, and Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan. I think it was taken sometime in the autumn of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And where? Can you see from the background what it may be?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: You can't see it on this photograph, but I saw a better copy of the photograph, and on it one can see that it was taken in the centre of Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Milanovic, did you review some videotapes during the proofing sessions and subsequently some stills from the videos?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you also indicate then on a separate sheet whom you recognised?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The first video, did it relate to a news conference on the 25th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's Exhibit -- tab 22 and 23 in Exhibit 549, and we do not like to play the video because it simply shows who is present, but the witness has indicated on a document that he signed and also dated, he has indicated the people that he saw in the video. We have the stills here and also his comments on who is who, and it's at the moment on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, it's tab 23. If you look into your binder, it's tab 23. And is that what you actually found from the video?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the next video that you actually saw was related to a footage from a meeting on the 20th of November, 1991, in Velepromet in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, in this case it is Exhibit 458, tabs 19.2 and 19.3.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you also -- if you now look at the screen, did you produce also a document indicating again which persons you recognised?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the video. On the first photograph I recognised --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can all see it. You do not need to repeat it. But that is document that's signed by you and produced by you together with assistance from the office here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: That is that document, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I don't understand what this is about. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff said that this was a meeting that took place on the 20th of November in Vukovar, and here some men can be seen who are standing there to have their photograph taken. Is that the photograph she was referring to? Who was attending this meeting in Vukovar? I simply cannot decipher it from this examination. What is the witness claiming? Who attended that meeting in Vukovar on the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: All this witness is doing is identifying these people in the photographs. If there is anything more that Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. wants to ask him or you want to ask him in due course, you can both do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask any questions in relation to this meeting. I just wanted him to identify the people that he saw on the video when he reviewed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the next video, it's tab 24 and tab 25 of the Exhibit 549, and it relates to a parade and press conference in Baranja in January 1992. Mr. Milanovic, did you review that video in which General Bijorcevic gave a speech?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did review the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we do not want to play the speech of Mr. Bijorcevic. What we have done is we have provided a page with a transcript of what he said, and it was given to the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Where is that now? We've got the photographs, 24, and the -- I'm sorry, 25.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: 25 are the photographs, and 24 is the video. And we have actually provided also a sheet --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- with the speech of Bijorcevic, which is actually also cited in the statement and in the proofing summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It can go in at 24.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And we therefore do not want to play the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But you reviewed the -- you reviewed the tape, and you produced again a document in relation to the people that you recognised; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, and you can also see that the witness has indicated himself as well as a participant on 51.07. It's just here in Sanction. He has indicated himself being present there. That should be enough for this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you have described in your statement, and I have to say here that it is and is forgotten in the proofing summary at paragraph 77 and 78 of the statement, you have described how you participated in a session of the extended Presidency on the 1st of February, 1992, and my question is: Do you recall what General Adzic said to promote the Vance Plan, to make it acceptable to the people in the region, in your region?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that meeting in the palace of the Federation. I don't need to enumerate all those present because it's written here. Among others, General Adzic spoke, and I think at the time he was Chief of Staff of the Main Staff of the army of Yugoslavia or the Yugoslav People's Army, and he was trying to assure and persuade those of us present to accept the Vance Owen Plan and that the army stood behind it, and should the Croats should attack us, they would help us.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have already mentioned and it's also described in your statement the arrival of the UN forces and what was done to prepare for this.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, it's in the -- it's the paragraphs 57, 79, and 80 of the statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have mentioned the officers, Colonel Bozo Kosutic, and Colonel Rajko Kovacevic being in charge of the blue brigades, and my question is: These officers, were they JNA officers and did they continue to be employed with the VJ and paid by them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were officers of the army of Yugoslavia, and they received a salary.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have also mentioned that the JNA left behind vehicles and weapons under this double-key system and how they were repainted? Who made these decisions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. What decisions?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned in your statement that the JNA left behind vehicles and weapons under this double-key systems. You said that military vehicles were repainted blue, that parts of the TO now became police staff, and my question was: Who made these decisions to do that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the Vance Owen Plan, the Territorial Defence and the army needed to take off their uniforms and put on civilian clothes. Only the command of the TO could remain active, incomplete, but they had to be in plain clothes. According to the Vance Owen Plan, it was permitted for two police brigades to be formed which would wear blue uniforms. In our country the police wear blue uniforms. And that they should be in the area. I also said the exact number of men, and as there was a shortage of men, then from the army and the TO some people transferred to special police units, and the permitted weapons were painted over in blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned a meeting in Karadjordjevo on the 24th of February, 1992, in your -- in your statement. Those steps to be taken, were they all discussed there on that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were discussed at the meeting as to how this should be technically carried out and how the blue brigade should be prepared so that they would guarantee the safety of the people in the area of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, because the army of Yugoslavia was withdrawing. The TO was being disbanded, and it was important that the people should have confidence in the two brigades that would be in that area of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Would you please have a look at tab 26 in the binder Exhibit 549. That's a plan for the demilitarisation and transforming of the 11th Corps of the army of the RSK. That is not now related to the arrival of the UN forces but to the Erdut agreement. Can you say to which -- when this document was actually compiled, because it has no date on it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: This document was most probably compiled in the second half of November 1995, after the signing of the Erdut agreement, because it is in the spirit of that agreement according to which the 11th Corps of the SBO needed to be demilitarised.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when you look at the second page of this document, at item number 8, there is a reference to 300 policemen from the Serbian MUP. What kind of unit is that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a unit, PJM, a special unit from the MUP of Serbia which was in the area and guaranteed safety to the people of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when did they come to the region and who commanded them? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you the exact date, but it must have been after the 5th of August, 1995. The commander was Major General Obrad Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In your statement and also already today, you mentioned the weapons that were left behind by the JNA and placed under the double-key system. You also gave the details of the amount of weapons and what kind they were. Who had the two keys?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: The one key was in the TO command or headquarters, and the other key was in the hands of the commander of the sector for the UN forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the RSK TO regain control over these weapons at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the attack of the Croatian army on Western Slavonia in May 1995, Croatia violated the Vance Owen Plan. It attacked the area, and in agreement with the UN forces, the weapons and artillery was taken over by the TO and an army was formed in the territory of the region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You also mentioned in your statement that despite the Vance Owen Plan, five TO brigades continued to exist in the region, and they were commanded by Colonel Sladojevic. To whom did Colonel Sladojevic answer? To whom did he report?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Which period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I'm referring to the period when there was the RSK. That's in 1992 through to his replacement.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: If we're talking about the taking over of weapons and artillery from the double-key system, the brigade and command existed, as I said, in civilian clothes. When the weapons were taken, they put on uniforms. And he was subordinated to the TO command in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did he also report to someone in Serbia or coordinate his actions with someone in Serbia, with the VJ? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let the witness answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My objection has to do with the question, because the question is leading. He's being asked whether he coordinated his activities with anyone else. At that time, there were no actions over there, so he couldn't be coordinating. There were no operations in the Srem-Baranja region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you would like to rephrase the question, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In the time period that Colonel Sladojevic was in charge of the TO, that is starting from 1992, did he coordinate with anyone in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: When Colonel Sladojevic became TO commander, up until to his replacement almost in 1995, there were no operations. His commander was in Knin. But he was on good terms with the Novi Sad Corps, and this, in my view, out of logical reasons, because the SBO was not physically linked to the lower part of Krajina, but it leaned on the area of responsibility of the Novi Sad Corps. It was adjacent to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In relation to funding and equipment of the TO, beginning actually in 1991, during 1991, did -- who financed and equipped the TO in 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't testify about the very beginning of 1991, but for the very end of it I can, as well as the beginning of 1992 until the Republic of Srpska Krajina was formed. It was financed in various ways. Partly by the economy of the region, the SBO, and aid did come from the army of Yugoslavia as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the TO continue to receive funding from the JNA or VJ later?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: It did receive it later, but since the formation of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, that is the 22nd of February, 1992, all this was done via Knin and then Knin would pass it on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you review a variety of documents related to financing, equipping, and training of either TO or police of the RSK during the proofing session?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I did review those documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We will now -- did you find them to be authentic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are authentic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we will now address some of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: First of all, Exhibit 327, tab 9. It's now all exhibits from the special bundle with the map on top of it, and it is here an Official Note on a meeting with Mr. Milosevic and others on the 12th of November, 1992. Did you know that such a meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that Colonel Stojan Spanovic was then Minister of Defence and that he said to me that a meeting had been held, but I did not know who had been present. And he also said that the mode of financing had been agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And looking at the document as such, is it -- when you look at the signature and the stamp and the format, is it authentic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: It is correct. I know the stamp, and I personally know Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mr. Spanovic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the mode of financing that is discussed here, partly through the VJ and partly through the Ministry of Defence, was that actually done in that way, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was being carried through.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 327, tab 14. It relates to the funding of the police. Do you know whether this was done in the way described from the -- through the Republic of Serbia, and is it an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: According to its letterhead, stamp, and signature, the document is a correct one.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next one is tab -- is 327, tab 17, and it's a document of the 28th of August, 1993, and refers to a sum of $60.000 US. First of all, the person Milan Tepavcevic receiving this document, who was he? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that at that time Tepavcevic was assistant head or deputy head of the state security service of Serbia. As for the document, I think that it is correct in terms of its letterhead and stamp. However, it was not signed by Martic himself; it was signed by someone else on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the background of this matter here described in the letter?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I remember an Assembly when Martic attacked the mentioned Dusan Orlovic, and this money went missing, that what was intended to be bought was not actually bought.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next document is Exhibit 352, tab 14, and it relates to a request for a unified credit and monetary system. Were you aware of the request for such a unified system?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that request because in 1992 it was a topical matter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what we looked at awhile ago, Martic's letter, when he says, "Within your possibilities, please give us help." Is there another tab 14 perhaps? This is the only tab 14 I have here. This is what it says here. Exhibit 327, tab 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's Exhibit 352, tab 14. That's a different document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, I don't want to stop you going through these, of course it's matter for you, but I just wonder, when they've already been produced, if we need go through them again. They may speak for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: In the interests of speeding things up.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can do that, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Were they marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, I think they were admitted, but the witness is actually closer, that's why I thought it may be necessary to repeat this exercise. So if not, then we simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If there are any matters arising, you can ask them --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- but for the moment, I suggest we move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But I want to ask him in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This document is directed to the Republics of Serbia and Montenegro, and not -- except for the bank, not to the federal organs. Why that? Why was that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that at that time, that was the 12th of May, 1992, the federal authorities did not function for reasons that are well known, because republics had seceded, and the entire monetary system and the budget was reduced to the government of Serbia and the government of Montenegro, and the government of Srpska Krajina addresses them directly, as well as the governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, this is a typical example of a question that is quite wrong and totally leading. This document pertains to the monetary system, and it is addressed, as you can see, to the governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia. That is an institution. It is the central bank which is responsible precisely for such matters. And of course it is also addressed to the government of the Republic of Serbia and the government of the Republic of Montenegro, but it is addressed to the federal authorities. The only federal authority in charge of this particular matter, the monetary system, the central bank. How can this question be put why it was not addressed to the federal authorities? But it was. It was addressed to the central bank, and it pertains to monetary matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, let the Prosecution put their questions; you can put yours. But as we say, I'm not quite sure the value of this exercise now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Just one more --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It is on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: One more question: Was the money of the RSK printed by the National Bank of Yugoslavia later on?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was printed at the mint, or I don't know the name of this institution but this is an institution of the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And was cash money transported from Yugoslavia to the RSK?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- but I would like to turn to one exhibit, and that's Exhibit 352, tab 15 -- 152. This document was discussed, but I think the witness can tell us the background of the proceedings here. It's an order by Zivota Panic in relation to the accepting and initiating conscript soldiers into the army of the RSK from Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know to which practice this document relates?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: The document shows that this happened in January 1993. I cannot say exactly, but I think that's when the Croats attacked the lower part of the Republic of Srpska Krajina. Was it the Miljevac plateau or was it the Medak pocket, I cannot remember exactly, but it is for sure that that is when the Republic of Srpska Krajina proclaimed a state of general mobilisation and sent a request to Yugoslavia for its military conscripts to be returned to the area of the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were refugees from the RSK, were they falsely recruited in Serbia? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were such cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have also reviewed a document that asked -- it was a letter of Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's 352, tab 156, but we do not need to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In this document, there was a reference to staff for the military justice system. Was -- did staff from the VJ, military prosecutors and legal staff, come to the RSK, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: They did. They certainly did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And was a military justice system established?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was any war crime ever -- any war crime trial ever conducted in these courts?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember for all of the Republic of Srpska Krajina, but in the SBO, no, but civilian courts were trying war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you know how many convictions were achieved and -- in relation to war crimes?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly. I remember one particular case in Baranja, one that I have truly remembered, but I couldn't remember anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have described the -- in your statement, and we're now at paragraph 50 in the proofing summary, Your Honours, in the statement it's paragraphs 91, you have described the cooperation between the -- with the JNA Novi Sad Corps and how it developed in the time. My question to you is: Did you also have direct access to the chief of staff of the VJ, in particular General Zivota Panic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, cooperation was good, and I did have contact with the chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How did this start, actually, this direct contact with Zivota Panic? When did it start and how?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, they weren't really frequent contacts, and they started -- I can't remember. One occasion when we met at a gathering, we exchanged telephone numbers, and occasionally we would talk to each other and see one another.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What would be the issues of the -- that you discussed? Can you give examples?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but it was always in the service of the defence of the territory of the SBO.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have described in your statement a contact with General Perisic in relation to 50 tanks that you requested and actually received. Did you ask for tanks only or also for the crews to man the tanks?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date now when I made the request for the tanks and when I received them, but I didn't ask for crews.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the tanks when they arrived, how did they get into the RSK without being noticed, and where were they deployed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Well -- well, normally we did this secretly. They were deployed in the territory of SBO, but all this was in the interests of defending the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have also described a conversation or, rather, a visit of General Perisic to the 11th Corps in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, it's omitted in the proofing summary. It's at page -- at paragraph 121 of the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have described -- you have already described an event in which you rejected the -- rejected 21 -- 20 VJ officers that arrived in the region, but I think that's something we have to lead live. In 1995, did you make a request for commanding officers to the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: This was in August 1995, but certainly after the fall of the lower part of Krajina, we requested officers from General Perisic, and he sent to us some 20 or so officers but not with the speciality we had requested. He sent those we didn't need. So we turned them back. We sent them back.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you make an order to this effect?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did give the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did Badza call you in this context?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he called me.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can you describe what happened? What did he say, and what happened afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: After that, when I had written the order for them to be returned, Badza called me up, saying that I should come to a meeting in Belgrade, and I did go to the meeting. And I arrived at the meeting, and Badza sent me to see Mr. Milosevic, and we had a brief meeting there. Mr. Milosevic asked me to the effect that Momcilo Perisic was complaining about me, that I had written an order about the officers. I explained what it was all about, and Mr. Milosevic said that he would talk to Perisic, that it wasn't quite the way he had put it as he had heard my side of the story, what the request was, what kind of officers had arrived, and why they had left.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did Mr. Milosevic actually know your order or did he have it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that he had it, had this order. Perisic probably gave it to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was your order reversed or was it upheld?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. My order was carried out, and it was only once it had been carried out that Perisic complained about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. That's understood. But after your conversation with Mr. Milosevic, was your order reversed or was it upheld?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember exactly whether it was upheld or carried out, but anyway, officers would come and go from our area.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have described in your statement your communication with the Serbian MUP and other Serbian officials to special telephone lines. Who established these lines?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but I think that men came from Serbia. Whether they used to work in the post office or in the MUP, I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were the telephone lines occasionally cut off, and if so, who did that and why?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were frequently cut off. When I would make a "error," relations would cool, and as soon as the line would break, I knew what it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was about.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you the only one in the region with such a special telephone that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure about that. Mr. Ilija Kojic may have had it, but I'm not quite sure. And he was Assistant Minister of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Would others come to your office to use that telephone line, calling officials in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: Occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have mentioned the Serbian state security people being present in the -- in the region, and in relation to Branko Glusica, I would like to know -- where did he have his office?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand. The office in the SBO or in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In the region, in your region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I wonder if in fact that would be a convenient moment, since we're going on to a different topic. It is time to adjourn. Mr. Nice, as I understand it, you want to interpose another witness, which means that this witness would have to come back for the rest of his evidence next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I address you about that in private session for a minute?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Tomorrow, then, Mr. Milosevic, it may be that the evidence of General Smith will be interposed, but as you've heard, you are to hear within the hour. And I want, Mr. Nice, to make sure that if you would make sure this evidence, this note gets through, information gets through to the accused as to which of the two witnesses he has to prepare, either this witness or General Smith. Now, I should also say this, that tomorrow Judge Robinson has to be away from the Tribunal on urgent personal business and cannot, therefore, be present here, but he will have had the opportunity, and we will consider together the appropriate order in relation of General Smith. We've got the material, I think I'm right in saying. You're not asking for the summary to go in but the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We're asking for the statement. The summary is a draft, but the general has already worked on it, very helpfully by electronic means with us, and so I don't think there are going to be too many further amendments, but there may be some.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And he's only available tomorrow, you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As I understand it. It was difficult to get a day, but of course we'll see what he'll do, given the problems that this witness faces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That we face. Very well. We will adjourn now. Tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 9th day of October, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
